text:
maria: Heads-up: noticed a perf regression on the 1.4.0 attention kernel roll last night. Large-chat benchmarks (8k context) show 12% higher tail latency and 6% more OOMs.
alex: Oof. Which OOM pattern? fragmentation or big chop?
maria: Mostly fragmentation + unexpected fallback to CUDA malloc inside the new kernel. Stack traces show allocator path switching.
sophie: Can you paste the repro commands?
maria: Repro: run `./perf/run_chat.sh --model rwkv-70b --seq 8192 --batch 2 --engine attention-v1` on the staging GPU pool.
ryan: I dug into the profile — kernel scheduling causes many short-lived big allocations (~10-50MB) during KV cache updates. The current allocator knobs (expandable_segments=true, max_split_size_mb=32, garbage_collection_threshold=0.2) were tuned for stable kernels; the new attention kernel interleaves allocations differently so those settings are suboptimal.
alex: That matches my local trace. Also saw the runtime overriding user env knobs for some kernels (we shadow user settings when kernel selects alternate arena). Might be the culprit.
maria: repro logs:
```
[2026-03-17 22:14:02] mem: total 48GB, used 43.1GB
[2026-03-17 22:14:03] alloc: request 42000000 bytes -> fallback to cudaMalloc
[2026-03-17 22:14:03] gc: triggered, reclaimed 12MB
[2026-03-17 22:14:04] OOM: allocation failed 42000000 bytes
```
ryan: Proposed immediate mitigation: bump max_split_size_mb to 256 for the new kernel path and increase garbage_collection_threshold to 0.6 so GC runs earlier. That reduces cudaMalloc fallbacks in my smoke runs.
sophie: Can we do a quick experiment patch that respects user-specified knobs unless kernel explicitly requests override? I worry about silent shadowing.
alex: Agreed. We should not silently shadow. Add a runtime warning: `allocator: kernel requests override of user knob expandable_segments=true -> applying kernel override for attention-v1` so we can audit.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: running canary on pool-staging-3 (2 GPUs) with patched allocator flags.
maria: Quick perf numbers after patch (canary): 8k seq, batch 2 -> p95 latency down 8%, OOMs from 6 -> 1 across 50 runs. Memory churn reduced.
ryan: Long-term: consider per-kernel allocation arenas + allocation intent tags. Kernels will hint expected lifetime/size (e.g., KV_UPDATE: short/med/large) so allocator can place in appropriate arena without changing global knobs.
sophie: I like per-kernel arenas. Also add a small periodic async scavenger that targets small free-list fragmentation every Ns requests instead of waiting for threshold.
alex: Action items: 1) PR to stop silent knob shadowing + warning log (owner: alex) 2) Canary patch with `max_split_size_mb=256` for attention-v1 (owner: maria) 3) Design doc for per-kernel arena + allocation tags (owner: ryan) 4) Add perf regression alert rule for p95 increase >5% (owner: sophie).
maria: I'll paste the minimal env override for the canary: `REDWOOD_ALLOC_MAX_SPLIT_MB=256 REDWOOD_ALLOC_GC_THRESH=0.6 REDWOOD_ALLOC_EXPANDABLE=1`
alex: Thanks — after canary we'll rollback or roll forward. If canary passes, we should push a short-lived fallback that keeps old kernel route on critical customers until we finish per-kernel arenas.
ryan: Also created a small script to reproduce fragmentation quickly: `scripts/frag_repro.py --kernel attention-v1 --iters 1000 --kv-size 64`
sophie: Nice. Once PRs land, let's run the nightly long-run (12h) on staging to validate no regression in cost (tokens/sec).
maria: TL;DR: regression caused by kernel allocation pattern + knob shadowing. Immediate fix in canary helps, long-term is per-kernel arenas + explicit logs for overrides. :thumbsup:
